c1-21.title: A big project
c1-21.story: Sofia's team had just reached a major [[milestone]]: the first version of their client's app was live. Before celebrating, her manager asked for a [[deep dive]] into why the project had run three weeks late. Sofia discovered that the client's [[billing]] department had never received the second [[invoice]], so the payment had stalled. She wrote a polite [[follow-up]] and attached the missing documents. Then she drafted a [[business case]] for automating the [[business process]] that had let the invoice slip through the cracks. Her manager approved it within an hour. To celebrate, Sofia treated the whole team to snacks from the [[vending]] machine, which, for once, didn't swallow her coins.

c1-22.title: Trouble at the office
c1-22.story: Anna's mama came home from the office looking exhausted. [[Top management|top management]] had just given her department an [[ultimatum]]: cut costs by twenty percent or face a restructuring. Rumors were spreading that [[middle management]] would be hit first, and her [[performance review]] was scheduled for Friday. On top of that, the [[compliance officer]] had found gaps in the team's [[compliance]] with new data rules. A colleague had also quietly reported [[harassment]] by a client, which mama took very seriously and passed on to HR. Taras suggested she set seven alarms to keep track of everything, but Anna laughed that this would be [[overkill]]. Instead, she helped her mama build a simple weekly planner, since good [[time management]] was clearly what the week required. By Friday, the review had gone well, and the restructuring was postponed.

c1-23.title: Dad buys a car
c1-23.story: Anna's dad finally decided it was time to replace the family's ancient car. At the [[showroom]], a salesperson explained that [[leasing]] would mean lower monthly payments than buying outright. Dad, however, was far more interested in an old [[off-road]] model parked in the corner. He crawled underneath to check the [[chassis]] for rust and asked whether the engine still had a [[carburetor]]. On the test drive, he pressed the [[accelerator]], and the engine roared impressively. Back at the lot, a mechanic used an air [[compressor]] to fill a soft tire. Taras noticed that a rear [[reflector]] was cracked, and the dealer agreed to replace it for free. Dad signed the papers with a grin, while mama simply rolled her eyes.

c1-24.title: A delayed flight
c1-24.story: Max and Sofia were flying home on a cheap [[charter]] when the captain announced a three-hour delay. Apparently, a faulty [[transponder]] meant air traffic control couldn't track the plane properly. Stuck at the gate, Max realized his charger wouldn't fit the local outlets, so he bought a [[converter]] at a kiosk. Sofia, meanwhile, was worried about her suitcase, which had already been lost in [[transit]] once that year. Through the window, they watched a rescue helicopter land, its [[rotor]] whipping up dust across the tarmac. A friendly pilot sitting nearby told them he had trained for exactly this kind of problem in a flight [[simulator]]. He also mentioned that his brother served on navy ships, where [[sonar]] was just as essential as radar. When boarding finally began, the gate agent called one passenger's name five times before marking him as a [[no-show]]. Max joked that the man had probably given up and taken the train.

c1-25.title: A lake adventure
c1-25.story: Last summer, Anna's family rented a [[camper]] and drove to a lake in the Carpathians. Taras, who had learned to paddle through [[scouting]], insisted on taking the [[canoe]] out first. Anna preferred to rent a [[SUP]], though she fell into the cold water twice in the first ten minutes. Dad warned them both to stay on the near side of the red [[buoy]], where the water was shallow and calm. Later that afternoon, a hidden rock scraped the [[keel]] of a fishing boat near the shore. Everyone rushed to help push it free. In the evening, they hiked up a hill and admired a stunning [[panorama]] of the mountains. Grandpa, who had gone [[skydiving]] at seventy, claimed the view from a plane was even better. Taras immediately asked if he could try it for his next birthday, and mama said firmly, "Absolutely not."

c1-26.title: Wonders of the world
c1-26.story: When Anna's grandparents retired, they decided to finally see the wonders they had only read about. Their first stop was Iceland, where they watched a [[geyser]] blast boiling water high into the air. A guide explained that [[magma]] deep beneath the island heats the underground water. In Egypt, Grandma was sure she saw a lake shimmering on the horizon, but it turned out to be a [[mirage]]. They took dozens of photos of the [[Sphinx|sphinx]] at sunrise. A few months later, they flew to Japan just in time to see the [[sakura]] in full bloom. On the way home, they spent a night in a restored [[chateau]] in France. Then they took a train through a Swiss [[canton]] famous for its cheese. Back in Kyiv, Taras asked which place was the best, and Grandpa simply said, "Home."

c1-27.title: A trip to the Gulf
c1-27.story: Lisa spent spring break in Dubai, one of the seven [[emirates|emirate]], where her aunt works as a nurse. On the first day, their guide pointed out a palace that belonged to a local [[sheikh]]. He also described how the city had grown from a small fishing village. In neighboring Qatar, he added, the head of state is known as the [[emir]]. At the hotel beach, Lisa noticed a sign politely reminding visitors that [[topless]] sunbathing was not allowed. In the old market, she got lost and was helped by a taxi driver, a [[Sikh]] from India who had lived in the city for thirty years. On the drive back, he told her stories about an old [[mystic]] who had once lived in the desert and spent his days in prayer. On her last evening, Lisa heard someone speaking Ukrainian at the airport café and turned around to find a [[compatriot]] from Lviv. They chatted happily until their flights were called and promised to keep in touch.

c1-28.title: New gadgets
c1-28.story: Max is obsessed with every new [[gadget]] on the market, so his birthday present was easy to choose: a tiny portable projector. Unfortunately, it came with the wrong [[connector]], and his laptop couldn't link to it. After some [[browsing]] on online forums, he found a [[how-to]] video that explained the problem step by step. The video was made by a [[dev]] at a large [[telecom]] company who posts tech tips on weekends. His clever [[hack]] needed nothing more than a cheap adapter and a change in the display settings. Within twenty minutes, Max was projecting a movie onto his bedroom wall. Later, Anna borrowed the projector for her [[e-learning]] course so she could watch lectures on a bigger screen. Max proudly declared it the best birthday present ever.
